doc.title: John LaPorta interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

title: The Jazz Composers Orchestra and the Mingus Workshop records
summary: A player-writer group organized by Bill Coss lasted about two and a half years; a recording was blocked by union costs, and afterward Mingus invited him to record the Jazz Workshop dates.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans

blocks.x: How did the Jazz Composers Orchestra come about?

Bill Kass, I don’t know whether you know that name or not, was editor for Metronome Magazine. Metronome Magazine is now defunct but it was the parallel of Down Beat during those years, was a very good friend of Mingus, and they talked about it and Bill kind of organized it. And the idea of it was that it was to be player-writer members. And this is what it was essentially. And we were together for about two and a half years. We put together three major concerts and they were well received by the musicians in New York City and the only thing that exists today are a few articles that were write-ups on the concerts. We were supposed to do a recording of a live concert, I think it was Savoy, and the New York union got wind of it and they insisted upon getting money for the whole concert in front. And since it was still monaural, the chances were good that
nothing would come out of the taping of the concert, so it was just prohibitive in terms of the cost of it. So it was never recorded, which was a shame.

About a month later, well that was the last concert we did, and it was just too much for me. I was the musical director of it and just kind of controlling all of these various human elements was just beyond me, I’d had enough of it. So I said look, somebody else can handle this, I’ll just play in it. And it just kind of fell apart. About a month later Mingus called me up and said, “Would you like to do a date?” I said “sure.” I went there, and the nucleus of the Composers Workshop was there, and that’s the way Mingus’ Jazz Workshop records came into play. I’m glad that he did it, because otherwise there would be no record of it.
